item.title: Robust Golden Ratio universality as a consequence of a circulant symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.13842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find a robust scenario for the emergence of the Golden Ratio (GR) dynamical universality class, characterized by the dynamical exponent $z \equiv \varphi=\frac{1}{2}(1+\sqrt{5})$. Previously, its emergence required fine-tuning of system parameters. Here, the GR universality class appears generically in a wide class of Markov processes as a consequence of a global, circulant symmetry of the flux Jacobian. This symmetry leads to GR universality in systems where the total number of conservation laws is odd and larger than three. We introduce a multilane exclusion process with Bernoulli stationary measure as a minimal, parameter-free model, which features GR universality for all conserved modes, most of which are doubly degenerate. Our predictions, based on mode-coupling theory generalized to treat degenerate conserved modes, are corroborated by large-scale Monte Carlo simulations.
item.dc:creator: Luka Paljk, Johannes Schmidt, Vladislav Popkov

item.title: Complex surface patterning in homo- and heteroepitaxial contexts: (simultaneous) step bunching and step meandering
item.description: arXiv:2604.13821v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We confront a meso-scale continuum model, archetypical for the heteroepitaxial context, with an atomistic Vicinal Cellular Automaton (VicCA), built as a homoepitaxial counterpart, to show that in (2+1)D complex surface instabilities are fundamental growth phenomena rather than context-specific artifacts. Our approach is to first construct a Ginzburg-Landau-type model, designed to extend the previously (1+1)D Tersoff-type models to (2+1)D. We complement the continuum approach with a discrete one - the VicCA, in which we use a novel version of the potential landscape for the diffusing particles - a double-well potential located at each step edge. Importantly, this framework also captures both step bunching and step meandering. While these behaviors are rarely treated together in earlier approaches, they naturally coexist in real materials. Thus we establish a cross-context correspondence at the level of obtained morphologies and morphology diagrams and, additionally, a multiscale perspective on the governing parameters, bridging the gap between the mesoscale and atomistic modeling.
item.dc:creator: Vassil Ivanov, Vesselin Tonchev, Marta A. Chabowska, Hristina Popova, Magdalena A. Za{\l}uska-Kotur
